concept_options.title: Why Everything Depends on One Factory
concept_options.hook: Every AI chip, every smartphone, every data center runs through one factory on a 36km² island. There is no backup.
concept_options.visual_approach: Progressive chokepoint-map build. Supply chain diagram constructs left-to-right (EDA → Fabless → TSMC → OSAT → OEM) as narration runs; TSMC node lights amber last and holds. Abstract convergence diagram shows Apple/NVIDIA/AMD/Qualcomm + AI data centers as source nodes converging via cyan routes into one amber TSMC/Taiwan chokepoint node. Stat cards overlay production share numbers. All flat vector, dark editorial, Asymmetric palette.
concept_options.target_audience: Operators, founders, analysts, systems thinkers — anyone trying to understand where AI hardware actually comes from
key_points: TSMC controls 90%+ of advanced-node chip manufacturing — no volume alternative exists until 2028+
NVIDIA has overtaken Apple as TSMC's largest customer in 2026 — AI demand has made the concentration worse
TSMC Arizona is <5% of leading-edge output — CHIPS Act spending doesn't solve this on any 5-year horizon
TSMC's 2nm yield is 65% vs Samsung's 30% — the moat is 30 years of accumulated process, not geography
CoWoS advanced packaging is sold out through 2026 — a second chokepoint inside the primary one
Morris Chang: building TSMC elsewhere is 'a very expensive exercise in futility'
concept_options.core_message: The most advanced technology on earth runs through one irreplaceable bottleneck — and nobody can build an alternative in time to matter.
concept_options.cta: If you want to map the systems that actually move AI hardware, the research stack is linked in the description.
grounded_in: 90%+ advanced node market share data point
TSMC 65% vs Samsung 30% yield data point
concept_options.why_this_works: The leverage point is undeniable and visually demonstrable. A supply chain diagram that narrows to one amber node IS the argument — viewers understand it before the narration finishes. Title engine hit: 'Why Everything Depends on [Bottleneck].' Strong news peg (Q1 2026 record revenue, NVIDIA overtaking Apple) and evergreen structural argument.

concept_options.title: The Moat Is a Process, Not a Place
concept_options.hook: The US is spending $52 billion to clone a factory. The factory's founder says it won't work — and the reason has nothing to do with location.
concept_options.visual_approach: Data journalism treatment. Opens on Morris Chang quote. Animated yield comparison bar (TSMC 65% vs Samsung 30% vs Intel 55%). Radial diagram: TSMC's 'one-hour ecosystem' of suppliers vs Arizona supply chain spanning 3,000 miles. Government spending stat cards (US $52B, EU €43B, Japan ¥3.9T). Skeptic narrative mode dominant.
concept_options.target_audience: Policy-aware operators, researchers watching CHIPS Act spend, founders thinking about supply chain exposure
key_points: TSMC's 2nm yield is 65% vs Samsung 30% — fabrication quality is not interchangeable
The 'one-hour ecosystem': every supplier and tool within 60 minutes of Hsinchu, 30 years in the making
$52B CHIPS Act + $43B EU Chips Act + Japan subsidies all underperform on TSMC's 10-year horizon
TSMC Arizona faces permit delays, workforce shortages, and no local supplier ecosystem
concept_options.core_message: You can't clone 30 years of accumulated process yield with a check — no matter how large.
concept_options.cta: The research tools and databases I use for this kind of systems mapping are in the description.
grounded_in: TSMC 65% vs Samsung 30% yield data point
concept_options.why_this_works: Contrarian hook targets active frustration about CHIPS Act spending. Yield data is the underserved explanation nobody has visualized. Different narrative mode (skeptic dominant) from Concept A.

concept_options.title: AI Has One Chokepoint. This Is It.
concept_options.hook: Every frontier AI model runs on hardware that passes through a single bottleneck. This is not a policy problem. It's a physics and economics problem.
concept_options.visual_approach: Minimal data-first treatment using Remotion built-in components only (zero image generation cost). Animated number opener: CoWoS capacity in wafers/month climbing vs demand. KPI grid: NVIDIA as TSMC % share. Bar chart showing TSMC vs Samsung vs Intel at advanced nodes. Operator mode dominant — fast, data-dense, no narrative padding.
concept_options.target_audience: AI practitioners, cloud operators, investors with direct exposure to AI hardware supply
key_points: CoWoS packaging sold out through 2026, demand growing 113% annually
NVIDIA now TSMC's largest customer — AI demand has overtaken consumer devices
Every major AI accelerator depends on one packaging process at one company
Q1 2026: $35.7B revenue, +35.1% YoY — TSMC's pricing power is strengthening
concept_options.core_message: The AI supply chain has a single point of failure that no amount of capital can fix on any near-term horizon.
concept_options.cta: Stack and tools in the description.
concept_options.why_this_works: Zero image generation cost — entirely free to produce via Remotion dataviz components. Fastest production path. AI-specific angle is differentiated from Concepts A and B.

selected_concept.rationale: Concept A is the strongest launch episode for Asymmetric: undeniable leverage point, iconic hero object (semiconductor wafer), clean 5-box diagram that collapses to one amber node, AI urgency with evergreen structural argument. Best title engine match. HyperFrames diagram-build approach is native to this content.
modifications: Production plan updated per operator correction: ComfyUI (local GPU) for image generation, ACEStep (local GPU) for music, Fish Speech (local GPU) as preferred TTS with ElevenLabs as explicit paid fallback only if Fish Speech is unreachable. Serial GPU execution order enforced. No concurrent local workloads.

voice_selection.rationale: Fish Speech is the preferred local TTS — zero API cost, local GPU, no external dependency. Requires VRAM to be freed from ComfyUI before starting. Registry showed unavailable during preflight because ComfyUI models were loaded at the time — this is a GPU scheduling issue, not a provider availability issue. Fallback order only if Fish Speech fails after VRAM isolation: elevenlabs → openai → google_tts → piper. User must approve any paid fallback before it is used.

music_source.mood_direction: Minimal electronic documentary pulse, restrained tension, no vocals. Slow-building, controlled, no dramatic swells. Asymmetric brand: music_volume=0.08, ducking_threshold=-4dB under narration.

stages.approach: Full script: 3 title options, cold open, 6 sections per brand structure (0:00–13:00), motion notes, chapter cards. Target ~1,950 words at 150 WPM for 13 min. Asymmetric brand rules enforced: leverage legible by 0:35, no state unchanged >4s.

Map each script section to diagram scenes. 3 reusable templates: supply-chain-flow, stat-card-overlay, geographic-convergence-map. TSMC node always amber. HyperFrames scene blocks declared with timing, content, animation beat.

stages.approach: Provider-block GPU scheduling — group jobs by loaded model stack to minimize VRAM unload/reload cycles. BLOCK A (ComfyUI): if ComfyUI models are already loaded, run all ComfyUI work first — still images, diagram-support images, any background video clips — then unload. BLOCK B (Fish Speech): start after VRAM freed, confirm health, generate full narration script, stop. BLOCK C (ACEStep): start after Fish Speech stopped, generate music, apply quality gate (discard if weak → silence), stop. Sequential jobs inside the same provider window are allowed and preferred. asset_manifest logs: provider block started, provider/service, assets generated, model/workflow used, start/end time, output path, failure/fallback reason if any, provider block ended, VRAM handoff to next provider.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: Local provider fails after VRAM isolation → report specific failure details, do not switch to paid provider without user approval. A provider is only considered failed if conflicting GPU services were unloaded first and it still failed. ComfyUI fails after isolation → openai image gen (paid, requires approval). ACEStep fails after isolation → silence (no music). Fish Speech fails after isolation → report to user, ask before using any paid TTS.

stages.approach: Lock cuts, overlays, subtitle burn, music mix. Music ducking: 0.08 volume under narration per asymmetric.yaml. SRT generated and synced to narration. render_runtime=hyperframes carried forward unchanged.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Fish Speech (local, free, GPU) vs ElevenLabs (API, ~$0.50, no GPU)
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Unload ComfyUI models, start Fish Speech, confirm health, then generate. Fish Speech is available when VRAM is freed — registry unavailable status at preflight was VRAM contention, not a provider fault. Use ElevenLabs only if Fish Speech fails after isolation — requires explicit user approval.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Fish Speech produces high-quality voice comparable to ElevenLabs for documentary narration. ElevenLabs has more voice variety and instant availability.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: ComfyUI images (local, free, GPU) vs OpenAI/Imagen images (API, ~$0.08–$0.16 per image)
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: ComfyUI is preferred. Only fall back to API providers if ComfyUI is unavailable — requires user approval.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: ComfyUI with a well-tuned workflow matches or exceeds API image quality for flat vector illustration. Requires GPU availability.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: ACEStep music (local, free, GPU) vs no music (silence)
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Attempt ACEStep generation. If output doesn't meet Asymmetric restraint bar (minimal electronic pulse, no vocals), proceed without music. Do not force a weak track.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: A well-generated minimal track adds 10–15% to perceived production quality. A wrong track actively damages brand trust.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Serial GPU execution (slower, ~20–40 min total) vs parallel external APIs (faster, ~5 min, costs money)
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Serial GPU execution per operator rule. Wall time is acceptable for production quality. Paid parallel is not the default.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Serial execution is slower but produces local-quality assets at zero marginal cost.

gpu_execution_order: BLOCK A — ComfyUI (if models already loaded, start here): still images → diagram-support images → optional video/background clips → save all outputs → unload ComfyUI models
BLOCK B — Fish Speech: start server after VRAM freed → confirm health → generate full narration → save outputs → stop Fish Speech

HANDOFF: all local GPU work complete → proceed to edit/compose
metadata.local_provider_failure_rule: A local GPU provider is only considered failed if: (1) conflicting GPU services have been unloaded, AND (2) the provider still fails to start or generate. Do not use paid external fallback until local isolation has been attempted and user approves the fallback.
metadata.concurrent_gpu_rule: FORBIDDEN — only one local GPU workload at a time. ComfyUI, ACEStep, Fish Speech, WAN, LTX, Hunyuan, comfyui_wan must never run concurrently.
metadata.provider_block_scheduling: Group asset generation by currently loaded model stack to minimize VRAM unload/reload cycles. If ComfyUI is already loaded, run all ComfyUI work first (still images + diagram images + video clips) before unloading. Then load Fish Speech for all narration. Then load ACEStep for music. Sequential jobs inside the same provider window are allowed and preferred. Do not rigidly order by asset type — order by provider residency.
metadata.operator_notes: This run avoids ComfyUI unless the allocator issue is fixed and verified. Use HyperFrames-native SVG/CSS visuals for wafer/EUV/Arizona/convergence scenes. Narration uses Fish Speech in chunked mode (25–40s chunks) with sequential generation + duration validation + concatenation per section. Asset order: author HyperFrames visuals first (CPU), then generate VO (GPU), then optional ACEStep music, then compose.
